items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: Made a lot of records with him, too. Under his name.

ctx.x: Hamp with a big band, that's right, Gene Krupa, Diz, Adderley--Cannonball, him and Nat Adderley, and so you remember some awful nice times working in there, in the Metropole. Well the one who really built that Metropole was Henry Red Allen. He had a number he used to do, 'Kiss the Baby.' People used to come from all over the world if they had a new date, to come in and holler up at Red, 'play 'Kiss the Baby.' And they'd play 'Kiss the Baby.'
Here's someone we really hadn't touched on.

items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: I remember some beautiful times in there with Red Allen... just everybody worked there.

ctx.x: And you were working opposite them?
Yes, I had my band in there then. Or was I with Red Allen? It may have been with Red Allen I don't know. One time I was with Red and then one time they were still there and I had my own group.
I see. We didn't talk about Hawkins at all. Did you know him very well?
